claims.text: The initial HfMoTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic.
As-cast equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperature, including approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is to replace part of the Hf with Zr, exemplified by Hf0.5MoTaTiZr1.5.
Hf0.5MoTaTiZr1.5 contains approximately 10 at.% Hf, 20 at.% Mo, 20 at.% Ta, 20 at.% Ti, and 30 at.% Zr.
Substitution of Hf by Zr will preserve a disordered, single-phase BCC solid solution.
Hf and Zr are both large refractory atoms, making the proposed BCC phase retention plausible.
Zr has a lower intrinsic density than Hf.
Replacing Hf with Zr will reduce the alloy's average atomic weight and mass per unit volume.
Both Hf and Zr contribute comparably to lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
The modified alloy will have lower density than the approximately 10.21 g/cm³ baseline.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength and ductility within approximately 10% of the baseline at room temperature.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength and ductility within approximately 10% of the baseline near 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is limited to room-temperature and approximately 1000 °C tensile or compressive loading of material retained in the as-cast condition without coatings or thermomechanical treatment.
The cited study examined equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr as part of an elemental-subtraction series.
A controlled experiment can compare density, phase constitution, strength, and ductility of Hf0.5MoTaTiZr1.5 against the original alloy at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is rejected if density does not decrease significantly or if yield strength or ductility decreases by more than 10% at either test temperature.
